properties.name: A test that writes a large design outside a write unit runs about 200 times slower in the workspace build, where full-text is on, than in the no-RocksDB build its author checks locally
properties.statement:
OBSERVED 2026-10-26, PR #802 (run 40267048719): the job "workspace + real-binary instruments" was cancelled at its 60-minute limit. The two 100,000-step deep_walks tests ran from 04:07 to 05:03 and never finished. In the same run, "core gates (no RocksDB)" passed them in about 20 s, and main's whole workspace job takes about 26 minutes.

MEASURED on this laptop, debug, building the same chain with unbatched node and edge writes:
- full-text off: 1,000 steps in 0.59 s; 4,000 steps in 1.96 s.
- full-text on: 1,000 steps in 118.5 s; 2,000 in 257.6 s; 4,000 in 534.8 s.
- The walk itself took the same time either way (0.03 s to 0.17 s).
- The 200 generated designs: 4.8 s with full-text off, 179.8 s with it on.

CAUSE (code read, matching the measurement): outside a batch, every node write commits the Tantivy index and reloads its reader (foundation text commit: "Forces a reader reload"; clear_graph, and the node paths in batch.rs, commit when no write buffer is open). `cargo test --workspace` builds reflow2-core with `fulltext` on, because reflow2-mcp asks for it, so a core unit test pays that cost there and nowhere else. The PR's local checks ran reflow2-core only with --no-default-features, which is the fast path the 2026-10-12 small-changes practice uses.

FIX in #802: the test chain is written in one write unit (begin_unit/commit_unit), as a served call writes. After the change the four deep_walks tests pass with full-text on (250 s, mostly the unbatched generated designs) and with it off (74 s).

NOT ESTABLISHED:
- Whether any served path writes many nodes outside a unit. Served calls each run in one unit, so they pay one commit per call.
- Whether other existing tests pay the same cost unseen.
- The batched chain was not re-run against main's recursive walks. The batch changes only how writes land, not what the walks read.
